rationale_highlights: There is no question that Mr. Armbruster has suffered because of his aboriginal status.
Unique systemic and background factors have contributed to Mr. Armbruster's inability to function in a civil society.
In my view the Gladue case requires the Court to take these facts into account in determining a fit sentence.
our analysis of the fitness of Mr. Armbruster's sentence must take into account the new method

crime_highlights: She was selling crack cocaine in the Main and Hastings area of Vancouver to support her own habit.
On 8 October 1999 she had 75 rocks of crack cocaine weighing 9.2 grams.
having sold one piece of crack cocaine to an undercover police officer for $10
the respondent was under the control of her former boyfriend who was taking the profit from her trafficking activity
rationale_highlights: although the sentence was lenient, it was appropriate in the circumstances of this offender
She is an aboriginal person and therefore entitled to the special consideration mandated by s. 718.2(e) of the Criminal Code.
a restorative approach should be fully explored and incarceration considered a last resort
This is also a case that called for a large measure of compassion.
note: Drug trafficking; no victim harm described.

crime_highlights: Ms. Courtereille attended the apartment of the deceased, Antoine West.
she commenced hitting Mr. West with a leg from a coffee table leaving him with some 40 contusions, abrasions and lesions
Ms. Courtereille then stabbed Mr. West some 40 times, his death resulting from the 7 wounds to the area of his heart and lungs.
The brutality and viciousness of the attack was evidenced by the blood splattering which occurred throughout much of the apartment.
rationale_highlights: In my judgment the circumstances of this aboriginal offender played a very substantial role in getting her to the stage where this offence was committed.
the learned trial judge did not refer to the special attention required to be given to the circumstances of aboriginal offenders
The failure of the trial judge to come to grips with the problems that this offender encountered in her life before the offence
I would give leave to appeal but I would allow the appeal and reduce the period of ineligibility down to 12 years.
note: Rationale passage slightly over 350 words; conclusion is the parole ineligibility reduction.
